issues.title: Sidecar partial mutation leaves internal self-contradiction
issues.details: The sidecar's top-level metadata fields (plan_path, canonical_sidecar_path, plan_sha256) were updated to r001, but the embedded review content (raw_review_excerpt at line 50, review.issues at line 152, review.technical_reality at line 187) still describes the pre-rename paths as the current state. For example, review.technical_reality says 'Sidecar internal plan_path still reads .../archon-piv-loop-codex-v2.prd.md (absolute path, pre-rename)' while the actual plan_path field now reads the r001 path. The file contradicts itself.
issues.suggested_fix: This is a documentation-level inconsistency, not a handoff blocker. If the sidecar is treated as historical provenance from round 1, add a top-level annotation field (e.g. metadata_updated_post_review: true) to signal that the metadata was corrected after the review text was written. Alternatively, if a clean sidecar matters, regenerate via a fresh review pass at the r001 path.

verification_gaps: plan_sha256 was updated but cannot be independently verified against the current PRD content — no shell/hash computation available in this review lane
run_claude_peer_review.py --check-only was not independently run; the claimed pass is based on caller assertion and consistent-with file inspection, not reproduction
Orchestrator consumer code for sidecar intake is outside this repo — cannot verify whether the embedded review text contradiction would cause downstream confusion
recommended_fixes: Consider adding a top-level annotation field to the sidecar (e.g. metadata_updated_post_review: true) to clearly signal that top-level metadata was patched after the embedded review was written, preventing future readers from trusting the review text's path claims as current
